'''Custo Ramak''' was a famous [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Author/Legends|author]] who [[Death/Legends|died]] many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. His deathbed work, ''[[Nights of Ryscate and Diamonds]]'', was a deeply sentimental and widely celebrated account of his life in [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet City]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. After his death, Ramak's [[Funeral/Legends|funeral]] ashes were compressed into<ref name="Coronet City" /> a [[soul diamond]],<ref name="Suns">''[[Suns of Fortune]]''</ref> as was Corellian custom, and it was put on display in the [[Museum of Fine Art]] in Coronet.<ref name="Coronet City" /> His remains were stolen during the [[Battle of Corellia]] during the [[Galactic War]] between the Republic and the Empire, and rumors abounded that they had surfaced on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="Shadow">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=crewskill|Treasure Hunting|Dust to Diamond}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Custo Ramak was first mentioned in the Codex entry for Coronet City in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] in [[2011]].<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>
